Bug_Details:
Double.longBitsToDouble converts the bit pattern into its corresponding floating-point representation. The method expects a 64-bit
long argument to interpret the bits as a double value correctly.
When the argument is a smaller data type, the cast to long may lead to a different value than expected due to the interpretation of
the most significant bit, which, in turn, results in Double.longBitsToDouble returning an incorrect value.
Noncompliant code example
int i = 0x80003800;
Double.longBitsToDouble(i);   // Noncompliant - NaN
Compliant solution
long i = 0x80003800L;
Double.longBitsToDouble(i);   // Compliant - 1.0610049784E-314
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by passing an integer value to the Double.longBitsToDouble method instead of a long value. This causes the method to interpret the bits incorrectly, leading to an unexpected result such as NaN.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method of the DoubleBitsBug class, which incorrectly uses an integer instead of a long in the Double.longBitsToDouble method. The assertion checks for the correct result, but since the input is incorrect, the result is NaN, causing the test to fail.
